articles.title: Tabilo y Barrios - Pedro Martínez y Munar: horario y dónde ver hoy en TV los partidos del Chile - España de la Copa Davis
articles.standfirst: España, a cerrar el pase a la final
articles.summary: España, a cerrar el pase a la final
articles.body: La selección española de Copa Davis busca este domingo rematar el trabajo en tierras chilenas y certificar su billete a la Final a 8 de Bolonia tras un arranque inmejorable. La joven pareja formada por Dani Mérida y Rafa Jódar protagonizó una jornada de sábado memorable al firmar dos brillantes victorias individuales sobre Alejandro Tabilo y Cristian Garín, respectivamente, otorgando una valiosa ventaja de 0-2 al equipo capitaneado por David Ferrer y dejando la eliminatoria a solo un punto del triunfo definitivo. El cruce se reanuda con el duelo de dobles en el que Pedro Martínez y Jaume Munar, invictos como pareja en la máxima competición por países, se medirán al tándem local compuesto por Alejandro Tabilo y Tomás Barrios. En caso de ser necesario para resolver la serie, la jornada continuará con los hipotéticos compromisos individuales entre Alejandro Tabilo y Rafa Jódar, seguido del choque entre Cristian Garín y Dani Mérida, en una pista central llamada a apretar al máximo. El partido entre Alejandro Tabilo y Tomás Barrios contra Pedro Martínez y Jaume Munar, correspondiente al punto de dobles de la Copa Davis, se disputa este domingo 20 de septiembre a las 17:00 horas (horario peninsular español). El encuentro entre la dupla chilena y el conjunto español se podrá seguir en directo por televisión a través de los canales M+ Vamos (dial 8) y Deportes 2 por M+ (dial 64) en Movistar+. Sigue toda la actualidad de la Copa Davis, el minuto a minuto del partido y la última hora del Chile - España en MARCA.com y escucha la retransmisión en directo en Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Aliassime conduce a Canadá a la fase final de la Copa Davis con récord de espectadores en Quebec
articles.standfirst: Francia vuelve a fracasar ante un rival que tenía las sensibles bajas de Shapovalov y Diallo
articles.summary: Francia vuelve a fracasar ante un rival que tenía las sensibles bajas de Shapovalov y Diallo
articles.body: Canadá acompañará a Italia (campeona), Corea del Sur, Austria y la República Checa en las finales de la Copa Davis de Bolonia (24 al 29 de noviembre). El conjunto norteamericano se convirtió la pasada madrugada en el quinto país clasificado gracias a la victoria de Felix Auger-Aliassime ante Arthur Rinderknech, por 4-6, 7-6(5) y 6-4. Aliassime, que ya había dado el segundo punto de la eliminatoria ante Quentin Halys y que se vio obligado a jugar también el dobles, hizo olvidar las sensibles bajas de Denis Shapovalov y Gabriel Diallo. Francia fracasa una vez más en una formación en la que no estuvo Arthur Fils, el tenista galo mejor clasificado. A pesar de nombres tan desconocidos como Duncan Chan y Liam Draxl, los canadienses pueden presumir de haber batido su récord de espectadores en una serie. Y es que en el estadio Videotron de Quebec se dieron cita 11.697 aficionados con ganas de tenis y de ver ganar a los suyos.

articles.title: World Team Cup: Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid win fifth title for Great Britain
articles.summary: Great Britain become World Team Cup champions for the fifth time as Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid secure a 2-1 victory over Japan in Florida.
articles.body:
Great Britain became World Team Cup champions for the fifth time as Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid joined forces to secure a 2-1 victory over Japan in Florida.

Japan were the defending champions of the competition, which is the wheelchair tennis equivalent to the Davis Cup and Billie Jean King Cup.

However, Hewett and Reid ensured Britain got their hands back on the trophy with a 6-1 6-2 win in the deciding doubles match against Tokito Oda and Daisuke Arai.

"We're really happy to get the title back," said Reid, who was also part of the World Team Cup-winning squad alongside Hewett in 2015, 2019, 2023 and 2024 .

Hewett added: "It's the first time it's come down to the deciding doubles for us, so I'm just really happy that we got over the line.

"It's always a privilege to play for your country and there's been a great atmosphere and team spirit again this week between all the lads."

Reid got Britain off to a winning start on Saturday with a commanding 6-2 6-2 victory over world number 21 Arai, who he has now beaten in all five encounters between the pair.

The start of the second singles match was then delayed because of extreme heat in Orlando, with Hewett and Oda returning to court six hours later when temperatures had cooled.

Just a week after beating the world number one in the singles final of the US Open, Hewett was unable to repeat his feat as he fell to a narrow 6-4 7-5 loss.

"I'm a bit disappointed that it wasn't a 100% day after my loss in the singles, but it was a really high-level match and just came down to a few points in both sets that could have gone either way," he said.

However, Hewett bounced back in the doubles alongside Reid as Britain, who also had 21-year-old Ben Bartram in the team and were captained by Martyn Whait, backed up their wins against South Korea and the Netherlands earlier this week.

articles.title: Zverev y un buen dobles le valen a Alemania para luchar por el título
articles.standfirst: Los alemanes no fallaron ante Croacia en Halle gracias a los dos puntos de su número 1
articles.summary: Los alemanes no fallaron ante Croacia en Halle gracias a los dos puntos de su número 1
articles.body: Para ganar la Copa Davis, en el actual formato, vale con un gran jugador de individuales y un buen dobles. Alemania tiene eso y estará en la fase final de Bolonia (24 al 29 de noviembre). Verdugos de Croacia en la pista dura de Halle se unen en en cartel a Italia (campeona), Austria, Corea del Sur, República Checa y Canadá. Alexander Zverev, que ya había ganado su primer partido el sábado, dio la puntilla a los croatas tras vencer a Dino Prizmic, por 6-2 y 6-4. Su victoria valió la clasificación entre los ocho mejores porque antes Kevin Kravietz y Tim Puetz superaron a Mate Pavic y Nikola Mektic, por 7-5 y 6-2. Alemania, con un Sascha que tiene entre ceja y ceja la Ensaladera que le falta, será una de las cuatro cabezas de serie en el sorteo del cuadro de las finales que se efectuará este martes. Italia es otra que tiene garantizada su condición de favorita por lo que ambas potencias no pueden cruzarse en los cuartos.

articles.title: Davis Cup 2026: Henry Patten & Neal Skupski win as Great Britain beat Ecuador to reach 'Final Eight'
articles.summary: Great Britain will play in the Davis Cup Finals for the first time since 2023 after claiming a 4-0 win against Ecuador in London.
articles.body:
Great Britain have reached the Davis Cup Finals for the first time since 2023 after sealing a 4-0 win in their qualifying tie against Ecuador.

Henry Patten and Neal Skupski booked Britain's ticket to November's 'Final 8' event in Bologna with a 6-3 6-4 win over Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo in the doubles at London's Copper Box Arena.

That gave Britain an unassailable 3-0 lead after wins on Saturday for Toby Samuel and Arthur Fery in the singles , before Harry Wendelken, a late call-up to the team after Cameron Norrie withdrew injured on Friday, wrapped up the best-of-five tie by beating Angel Veliz 6-2 6-3 on his competition debut.

"Three years - it feels like quite a long time," Britain's captain Leon Smith told BBC Sport.

"To do it in three straight rubbers is really good and I'm actually delighted for the guys to look forward to something at the end of the year."

Even against underdogs Ecuador, whose singles players were both ranked outside of the world's top 200, there were doubts if Smith could lead Britain back to the knockout stages given his inexperienced team in London.

Jack Draper ended his difficult season early , while Jan Choinski and Jacob Fearnley were both unavailable through injury.

Smith was then dealt a late blow when British number two Norrie pulled out on Friday after feeling pain in his arm during a practice session.

However, Samuel - after a breakthrough season that has seen him rise from outside the world's top 250 to 95th in the rankings - stepped up on his Davis Cup debut.

Just weeks after winning his first Grand Slam match at the US Open, the 24-year-old overcame nerves and fought back from a set down to beat Andres Andrade 4-6 6-4 6-1.

Fery, meanwhile, was making just his second Davis Cup appearance as the British number one claimed an assured 7-5 6-0 win over Alvaro Guillen Meza.

And with world number one Patten and new US Open champion Skupski to call upon for Sunday's doubles rubber, victory seemed to be well within Britain's grasp.

The pair, despite not playing together on the ATP Tour, combined effortlessly and did not face a single break point against the Ecuadorians.

"We are good friends off the court, which I think always helps, and we spend time with each other when we are on the tour anyway," Patten told BBC Sport.

"[LTA coach] Louis Cayer has created the British system so it's quite easy for Brits to play together - we both have a good idea of what the other player is going to do, where they are going to hit it, where they are going to move to."

The last time Britain made it to the quarter-finals in 2023, they fell to a 2-0 defeat by Novak Djokovic's Serbia, with Norrie and Draper both losing their singles matches.

"When you get to the Final 8 and you play one of the seeded teams, they are extremely strong," Smith said.

"[Italy's Jannik] Sinner could be back playing, [Spain's Carlos] Alcaraz has talked about his commitment to it at the end of the year, but you've got a chance. You try and steal one of the singles, and it goes to the doubles and you've got a good doubles team.

"There's a lot of excitement about it, it brings the team together again."

Three-time defending champions Italy qualified automatically as hosts for the Finals, which will take place in in Bologna from 24 to 29 November.

But the United States, who have won a record 32 Davis Cup titles, will be absent from the quarter-finals for a second successive year after they fell to a 3-2 defeat by the Czech Republic.

Christian Harrison and Austin Krajicek won their doubles match to give the Americans a 2-1 lead, but US Open runner-up Ben Shelton lost to Jakub Mensik before Jiri Lehecka sealed the tie for the Czechs with victory over Learner Tien.

South Korea advanced to the knockout stage for the first time on Saturday after beating India 3-1, while Austria joined them with a win over Belgium.

Canada, the 2022 champions, are also through after a 3-1 victory against France, while US Open champion Alexander Zverev won both his singles matches to help Germany to a 3-1 win over Croatia.

Spain are 2-0 up against Chile, with their qualifying tie resuming at 15:00 BST on Sunday.

articles.title: Davis Cup: Great Britain book place in Finals as Neal Skupski and Henry Patten victory over Ecuador
articles.summary: Neal Skupski and Henry Patten sealed Great Britain's place in the Davis Cup Finals in November, with a 6-3 6-4 win over Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo; it follows wins for Arthur Fery and Toby Samuel on Saturday, and means GB have reached the last eight for the first time since 2023
articles.body:
After singles victories for Arthur Fery and Toby Samuel on Saturday at London's Copper Box, Henry Patten and Neal Skupski clinched the tie at the earliest opportunity with a 6-3 6-4 win against Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo in the doubles rubber.

Britain therefore join three-time defending champions Italy, Canada, Czech Republic, South Korea and Austria in booking their spot for the eight-team event in Bologna.

It is the first time Leon Smith's side have reached the quarter-finals since 2023, when they were beaten by Novak Djokovic's Serbia in Malaga.

Whoever they draw - and as a non-seed they could find themselves up against the likes of Italy or Spain - they will face a much stiffer test than that provided by Ecuador.

The South American outsiders gave their all to the task in the hope of repeating their famous victory in the competition at Wimbledon in 2000 but were outclassed by Smith's men.

Britain are the leading nation in men's doubles and it would have been a huge upset had world No 1 Patten and new US Open champion Skupski not prevailed.

They had played together only once before - Patten's sole previous appearance - in a tie against Canada two years ago but gelled quickly, breaking serve at the first opportunity.

There was a moment of contention on the first point of the second set when umpire Marijana Veljovic ruled that Escobar had hit a volley while leaning across the net, awarding Britain the point.

The Ecuador duo put their anger aside to hold serve but a return winner from Skupski earned them another break in the ninth game, and Patten served out the victory.

"We're very, very happy to get it done in the first match," said Patten. "I think we played a good one."

articles.title: Tomas Barrios / Alejandro Tabilo - Pedro Martinez / Jaume Munar en directo | Eliminatoria de Copa Davis ante Chile, en vivo.
articles.summary: Tomás Barrios/Alejandro Tabilo - Pedro Martínez/Jaume Munar. 0-6, 1-5. Saca España. 30-30. Presiona Chile al resto. Iguales. Tomás Barrios/Alejandro T
articles.body:
Última hora del Chile - España de Copa Davis, en directo

Buenas tardes, bienvenidos al segundo día de la eliminatoria de Copa Davis ante Chile. Hoy tendremos en pista a los guerreros que intentarán certificar el pase a la Final a 8 de Bolonia (24-29 de noviembre). Para hacer un breve repaso, Rafa Jódar, Dani Mérida, Jaume Munar, Martín Landaluce y Pedro Martínez, son los seleccionados por David Ferrer para la batalla sobre la tierra de Chile. Por el combinado local, Alejandro Tabilo, Cristian Garín, Tomás Barrios Vera, Matías Soto y Benjamín Pérez lucharán bajo las órdenes de Nicolas Massú, por mantener la racha de 15 años sin ceder en una eliminatoria de Copa Davis como anfitriones. Hoy se disputará el encuentro de dobles.

Jaume Munar y Pedro Martínez buscarán ante Alejandro Tabilo y Tomás Barrios Vera el tercer y definitivo punto para España. Ayer, Dani Mérida tuvo un debut soñado ante Tabilo, con remontada al más puro estilo español incluida. Y posteriormente, Rafa Jódar, el otro debutante del equipo, puso el 2-0 superando con amplia claridad a Garín. Si el dobles no fuera suficiente, los dos madrileños volverán a saltar a pista. Rafa Jódar frente a Tabilo, los primeras espadas de ambos conjuntos, y por si hiciese falta el quinto partido, Dani Mérida intentará batir a Garín. Esperemos que con el dobles sea suficiente...

articles.title: Rafa Jódar, el segundo mejor debut en la historia de España
articles.standfirst: El madrileño cedió dos juegos, sólo superado por el triple 6-0 de Emilio Sánchez Vicario
articles.summary: El madrileño cedió dos juegos, sólo superado por el triple 6-0 de Emilio Sánchez Vicario
articles.body: "No voy a olvidar el debut en la Copa Davis", afirmaba Rafa Jódar tras sumar el segundo punto de la serie ante Chile tras derrotar a Cristian Garín, por 6-0 y 6-2. El madrileño, con 20 años recién cumplidos (los hizo el pasado jueves), se ha convertido ya en historia del tenis español en la máxima competición por países. Sólo Emilio Sánchez Vicario, en el partido contra el argelino Kamel Harrad, de la zona europea de 1984, supera la contundencia del debut de Jódar en una eliminatoria en juego. Emilio firmó un triple 6-0. Carlos Ferrer, en 1953, en otra serie zonal, también perdió dos juegos en su primer partido defendiendo a la selección nacional ante el israelí Mordechai Apel. El resultado en esa ocasión fue de 6-1, 6-1 y 6-0. Rafa sí es el mejor debut con la Armada en este siglo. El mejor estreno estaba en manos de Juan Carlos Ferrero, que cedió seis juegos ante Yevgeny Kafelnikov en la primera ronda del Grupo Mundial 2002. Juanqui se impuso por un triple 6-2.

articles.title: Novak Djokovic and Jelena Djokovic relationship story in 2026: Their journey from teenage sweethearts to a lasting marriage, family life and enduring partnership beyond tennis
articles.summary: International Sports News: Tennis and mutual friends helped bring Novak Djokovic and Jelena Djokovic together as children growing up in Serbia. The two slowly built a relationsh.
articles.body: Tennis and mutual friends helped bring Novak Djokovic and Jelena Djokovic together as children growing up in Serbia. The two slowly built a relationship, as friends initially, before they decided to date officially in 2005.The couple also had to deal with the difficulties of distance as Djokovic continued to play professional tennis while Jelena studied in Italy. Together they began a journey that would see them married and raising a family, with Jelena carving out her own role through the Novak Djokovic Foundation.Novak Djokovic and Jelena Djokovic’s love story in 2026Novak Djokovic and Jelena Djokovic’s love story started long before the Serbian tennis star became a global sporting icon; and the two met as teens in Serbia and connected through their shared environment and tennis links. Soon their relationship became romantic, and they started dating officially in 2005.Djokovic’s increasing professional commitments and Jelena’s education abroad shaped their early years together, while Jelena was studying in Italy on a scholarship, Djokovic traveled the world trying to establish himself on the professional tennis circuit. The geographical distance made their relationship difficult, but it didn’t stop it from happening.In 2013, after being together for several years, Djokovic proposed to Jelena in Monte Carlo. The couple wed in July 2014, shortly after Djokovic won his seventh Wimbledon title. Their wedding brought a new chapter, with their sporting and personal lives becoming more intertwined.Relationship milestoneDetailFirst connectionMet as teenagers in SerbiaOfficial relationshipBegan dating in 2005Engagement2013MarriageJuly 2014SonStefan, born 2014DaughterTara, born 2017Novak Djokovic and Jelena Djokovic’s early connectionThe relationship formed when Djokovic was still working his way to the top of professional tennis. The early years were a far cry from the highly publicized lifestyle of the family today, full of travel and uncertainty.Jelena’s education in Italy caused periods of separation in the couple’s life. Djokovic has spoken in the past about the challenges of sustaining their relationship during those years when travel to meet each other could be complicated by limited finances and his busy tennis schedule.Novak Djokovic and Jelena Djokovic build a familyFamily was a big part of the couple’s story after their 2014 wedding. Their son Stefan was born in October 2014 and their daughter Tara in September 2017. Many times and in public, Djokovic has spoken about the importance of family alongside his grueling sporting career.Jelena has also developed an identity through her philanthropy. She is a key figure connected to the Novak Djokovic Foundation and has been involved in initiatives especially focused on early childhood education and opportunities for children in Serbia.Novak Djokovic and Jelena Djokovic sustain their bondDjokovic and Jelena balance marriage, children, charity work and the pressures of top-tier sport decades after they first met. Jelena has often been spotted cheering on Djokovic at major tournaments, while also continuing her duties with the family foundation.So their story in 2026 is about far more than just Djokovic’s achievements on the tennis court. Novak Djokovic and Jelena Djokovic have built a family life alongside one of the most remarkable careers in modern tennis, from teenage friendship and a long-distance relationship to marriage and the raising of two children.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Munar y Martínez sellan el billete a Bolonia por la vía rápida
articles.standfirst: La pareja española tuvo bola de doble rosco ante Tabilo y Barrios y sentencia a Chile
articles.summary: La pareja española tuvo bola de doble rosco ante Tabilo y Barrios y sentencia a Chile
articles.body: Los 15 años de imbatibilidad de Chile como local y las 12 eliminatorias ganadas por Nicolás Massú en su banquillo ya son historia. El Parque Deportivo Estadio Nacional se preveía una caldera y se convirtió en un balneario en el que se paseó la selección española de la Copa Davis. Dani Mérida, Rafa Jódar y el dobles formado por Jaume Munar y Pedro Martínez han firmado un contundente 0-3 como visitantes. Por no haber no había ni la grada llena porque los aficionados locales ya intuían lo que iba a pasar después del resultado parcial de la primera jornada. España no es Paraguay, Perú, México, Venezuela, República Dominicana, Colombia, Ecuador, Eslovaquia, Kazajistán, Luxemburgo o una Serbia sin Novak Djokovic. Al rosco el sábado de Jódar ante Cristian Garín le siguió el 6-0 y 6-2 de Munar y Martínez ante Alejandro Tabilo y Tomás Barrios. El dúo español se mantiene invicto en la máxima competición por países. Tres partidos y otras tantas victorias. Y eso que no se juntaban a mitad de pista desde el Open de Australia en el mes de enero. La ruidosa hinchada chilena empezó como un campo neutral porque sus jugadores no les dieron razones de creer. El ruido llegó con tres juegos ganados por Tabilo y Barrios después de que Jaume y Pedro disfrutaran de una bola de doble 6-0. "El mérito es de los jugadores, que son muy buenos", decía Ferrer a los micrófonos de Movistar +. "Creo que hemos hecho un partidazo, lo que se ve en la pista es el ambiente que hay fuera", decía Munar. "Ellos estaban encogidos por el resultado y se han soltado después", comentaba Martínez. Martín Landaluce, a sus 20 años, se unió a la fiesta ganando el cuarto punto ante Matías Soto, por 6-2 y 6-3. El conjunto español conocerá este martes el cuadro de la fase final de Bolonia (24 al 29 de noviembre). Como cabeza de serie evitará a los otros favoritos en los cuartos.

articles.title: España será cabeza de serie en el sorteo este martes del cuadro de la fase final de la Copa Davis
articles.standfirst: La selección nacional es segunda en el ranking de la Federación Internacional de Tenis
articles.summary: La selección nacional es segunda en el ranking de la Federación Internacional de Tenis
articles.body: La selección nacional de la Copa Davis, que ha logrado este domingo su pase a la fase final de Bolonia (24 al 29 de noviembre), conocerá este martes su camino hacia la séptima Ensaladera de su historia. El quinteto de David Ferrer será uno de los cuatro cabezas de serie en el sorteo, a diferencia de la pasada campaña donde no dispusieron de esa condición. Eso significa que, si no varia la actual clasificación de la Federación Internacional de Tenis, evitarían a Italia hasta una hipotética final. La Alemania de Alexander Zverev también partirá entre las favoritas y el cuarto será la República Checa. Los italianos, vigentes campeones, además de anfitriones, irán por la parte alta del cuadro. Han levantado las últimas tres coronas en la máxima competición por países. El primer rival de España saldrá entre Canadá, Gran Bretaña, Corea del Sur y Austria. Cuatro de las ocho primeras selecciones del ranking no estarán en Bolonia: Bélgica (4), Estados Unidos (5), Francia (6) y Australia (8).

articles.title: "I was close to giving up": Aryna Sabalenka opens up on how she nearly ended her career in tennis amid the 2026 US Open loss
articles.summary: International Sports News: Aryna Sabalenka is easily one of the most talented athletes in the world even as she suffered a loss in the 2026 US Open. The 28 year old tennis star .
articles.body: Aryna Sabalenka is easily one of the most talented athletes in the world even as she suffered a loss in the 2026 US Open. The 28 year old tennis star is now gearing up for the China Open which begins in the next 10 days. But it seems, at one point in her life, Aryna Sabalenka wanted to give up on her stellar career.Aryna Sabalenka reflects on how she wanted to end her career in tennis but it is her family that kept her going through all the challenging daysA few months ago, in an interview with Vogue, the 4 Grand Slams title winner Aryna Sabalenka reflected on the challenges she faced in her life as she said, “There was a period when I was probably nine when I was close to giving up. But I saw how proud my dad was of me, and I didn’t want to disappoint him. And then I fell in love again with the sport, much more than before.”The 28 year old Belarusian professional tennis star added, “After I lost my father, it’s always been my goal to put our family name in the history of tennis…”Aryna Sabalenka continued, “Every time I see my name on that trophy, I’m so proud of myself, I’m proud of my family that they never gave up on my dream and that they were doing everything they could to keep me going.”While Aryna Sabalenka has had a successful career in tennis, she has often opened up about the challenges her family faced while raising her and her siblings.To make things worse, when the tennis star was just 13 years old, Aryna Sabalenka’s parents faced financial issues but they never let their children know what was happening.Despite the secrecy, Aryna Sabalenka has often spoken about how she and her siblings always knew the financial challenges their family was facing even though their parents tried to keep things private.Aryna Sabalenka reflects on witnessing her father’s death and how he could have been saved Later, in 2019, Aryna Sabalenka ended up losing her father to sepsis and she has often reflected on how he became a victim of medical negligence after he was refused to be taken to the hospital at the right time by paramedics.In the same interview with Vogue, the 4 Grand Slams title winner Aryna Sabalenka reflected on how she was training in Minsk during the November offseason when her father passed away.She said, “I was like, let me f–king carry him to the hospital myself if the ambulance isn’t taking him…They took him on the third day, and it was too late.”Despite the challenges she faced, Aryna Sabalenka kept her focus on her career and is one of the greatest athletes in the world today.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
